note: VARIETY: Zürich German (Züritüütsch). SPELLING: Dieth-lite phonetic — full spec in docs/course-optimization/swiss-german-convention.md (READ IT). Hard rules: no ß ever (ss); ch=/x/ (ich, cha, nöd, machä, Chind); long vowel doubled (Ziit, Aabig); st/sp→scht/schp before vowel (Schtei, bisch); ä for open-e; diminutive -li; no final -en (rede, machä, chömä). REGISTER: informal du throughout; Mundart is the complete spoken language, not 'casual German'. GRAMMAR: NO preterite — past is ALWAYS perfect (ich ha gseit, ich bi gsi); no genitive (use vo+dative); future = present. Verbs: bi/bisch/isch/sind; ha/hesch/hät/händ; wott/wottsch/wänd (want); cha/chasch/chönd (can); mues (must). These examples are authored by a competent source but are DIRECTIONAL — treat spelling/forms as the spec, verify final lexis with a native Zürich speaker.

examples.english: I want to speak Swiss German with you now.
examples.translation: Ich wott jetz mit dir Schwiizerdütsch rede.
